Ava: quick nsys run on prod-sim node g5-48. noticed a KV read/write imbalance during the fused-attn path, uploading trace
perf-bot: nsys job 9243 completed: s3://redwood-artifacts/nsys/9243.qdrep — perfetto: https://perfetto.app/trace/9243 (sampling + timeline) :white_check_mark:
Sam: can you paste the kernel timeline or a short summary? which kernels dominate the time slice?
Ava: timeline snippet: flash_attn_fwd_v2 (fused) ~42% total runtime, kv_read_write_shard ~33%, several memcpy/chunk-copy spikes ~5-7%. nsys command used:
```
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn --sample=cpu --output=9243 
--capture-range=kernel -- ./run_inference --profile-mode
```
Riley: hmm — does kernel selection choose fused-attn for short seqs? our batching heuristics prefer fused for seq <= 256 right now. could be that mixed read/write batches cause bank conflicts when fused kernel tries to keep everything in-register.
Ava: exactly. fused path is faster in pure compute but when KV writes interleave it causes membank contention. we see SM occupancy dip and L2 write-backs spike when writes hit hot shards.
Jamie: can we get nvprof/perf counters to confirm L2 / dram write amplification? i'd like a per-kernel counter set (gld/gst, l2_wb, dram_throughput). also a perfetto topdown view would help.
Ava: attached nvprof counters in the artifact bundle (grep for "NVPROF_COUNTERS"), perfetto shows repeated small write bursts aligned with kv_write kernels. key observations: L2 write-back spikes align with kv_write_shard, and flash_attn shows warp stalls right after those spikes. :thinking:
Sam: proposal: 1) serialize KV writes per-shard with a small coalescing window (2-4ms) to reduce write bursts; 2) change kernel selection: if batch has >10% write ops, force non-fused flash variant (less register pressure, more tolerant of interleaved memory ops); 3) run A/B using canary fleet. thoughts? :+1:
Ava: will run ablation. plan: a) implement per-shard write queue + coalesce, b) add kernel selection override flag for mixed-RW batches, c) run nsys sample + perf counters, d) measure p50/p99 latency and tokens/sec. scheduled job 9248.
perf-bot: Experiment 9248 queued on canary pool. ETA ~30m. :hourglass:
Sam: if results look good we can add an optimizer rule in runtime: detect RW fraction > threshold -> switch kernel + enable serialization. also add telemetry for kv write burstiness so we can autotune threshold.
Ava: noted. i'll upload raw traces and a short summary once experiments finish. thanks all.
